default.title: FOOD CRAVING
default.speaker: Food app
default.intro: After college. Turf cricket with friends tomorrow: ₹100 each.
default.text: A food app pings: 'Biryani ₹300, here in 20 min!' The shop next door has chips for ₹20.

pocket_money.title: FOOD CRAVING
pocket_money.speaker: Friend
pocket_money.intro: Mom gave this month's money yesterday. Turf cricket tomorrow: ₹100 each.
pocket_money.text: Your friend scrolls a food app: 'Biryani ₹300, let's order!' Chips at the canteen cost ₹20.

scholarship.title: FOOD CRAVING
scholarship.speaker: Classmates
scholarship.intro: The allowance just landed. Turf cricket with the class tomorrow: ₹100 each.
scholarship.text: 'Allowance day! Order ₹300 biryani on the food app to celebrate!' Chips at the canteen: ₹20.

earner.title: FOOD CRAVING
earner.speaker: Food app
earner.intro: Payday at the shop. Turf cricket tomorrow: ₹100 each.
earner.text: Tired after your shift. The food app flashes 'Biryani ₹300, free delivery!' Chips at your shop: ₹20.

choices.lesson: Tasty today, but the money for tomorrow's match is gone. A want only works if it fits the month.
choices.hint: What else did you want to do this week?

choices.lesson: A small want that fits, and tomorrow's match is still on. That's needs vs wants done right.
Sharing halved the cost. Still ₹150 on a want, so check it leaves room for the match.
Saving matters, but food is a need. Skip the wants, not the needs.

default.title: MONTH PLAN
default.speaker: Your wallet
default.text: Bus pass due on the 5th, a phone recharge, and a friend's birthday treat on the 10th. What comes first?

pocket_money.title: MONTH PLAN
pocket_money.speaker: Your wallet
pocket_money.intro: Mom hands over this month's money.
pocket_money.text: Bus pass due on the 5th, data running out, and Sana's birthday treat on the 10th. What comes first?

scholarship.title: MONTH PLAN
scholarship.speaker: Your wallet
scholarship.intro: The allowance has to stretch till next term.
scholarship.text: Bus pass due on the 5th, a recharge, and Imran's birthday treat on the 10th. What comes first?

earner.title: MONTH PLAN
earner.speaker: Your wallet
earner.intro: Wages are in. Part already went home.
earner.text: The rest covers your bus pass on the 5th, a recharge, and Kiran's birthday treat on the 10th. What comes first?

effects.label: Bills paid on time, ₹100 birthday gift

choices.lesson: Needs first, then a set amount for fun. Planning didn't cancel the party; it made room for it.
Fun first left the bus pass short. When bills are paid late, they usually cost extra.
choices.hint: What's due on the 5th?

choices.lesson: With no plan, ₹20 here and ₹50 there are gone by week 3.
choices.hint: Which of these can't wait?

choices.lesson: Bills are safe, but you didn't need to miss out. A plan can include a small fun budget.

default.title: FESTIVAL SALE
default.speaker: Shopkeeper
default.intro: Festival week at Laad Bazaar. You have ₹1,000 of festival money for new clothes.
default.text: The first shop: 'Kurta ₹800, last piece, today only!' Three more shops are down the lane.

pocket_money.title: FESTIVAL SALE
pocket_money.speaker: Shopkeeper
pocket_money.intro: Sankranti: relatives gave you ₹1,000 for new clothes.
pocket_money.text: First shop at Laad Bazaar: 'Shirt ₹800, last piece, today only!' Three more shops are down the lane.

scholarship.title: FESTIVAL SALE
scholarship.speaker: Shopkeeper
scholarship.intro: Eid is coming. Family set aside ₹1,000 for your new clothes.
scholarship.text: 'Kurta ₹800, final price, last piece!' says the first shop near Charminar. Three more shops are down the lane.

earner.title: FESTIVAL SALE
earner.speaker: Shopkeeper
earner.intro: Diwali: the shop owner gave you a ₹1,000 bonus for new clothes.
earner.text: First shop: 'Shirt ₹800, today only!' The lane behind Charminar has three more shops.

choices.lesson: 'Last piece, today only' is a sales trick. Two shops down, the same style was ₹550.
choices.hint: How many shops did you check?

choices.lesson: Ten minutes of comparing saved ₹250. That's compare before buying.
A 'deal' on things you don't need isn't saving. You spent more than you had.
choices.hint: Did you need three?

effects.label: No new clothes for the festival

choices.lesson: Saving is safe, but festivals matter too. Compare, buy smart, and save the difference.

default.title: SAVING GOAL
default.speaker: Your wish list
default.text: You really want new earphones: ₹600. This month's money is in your hand. What now?

pocket_money.title: SAVING GOAL
pocket_money.speaker: Your wish list
pocket_money.text: Your old earphones broke. New ones cost ₹600. This month's money just came from home.

scholarship.title: SAVING GOAL
scholarship.speaker: Notice board
scholarship.text: An exam fee of ₹600 is due in three months. The allowance just landed in your account.

earner.title: SAVING GOAL
earner.speaker: Your wish list
earner.text: A second-hand cycle (₹3,000) would make deliveries faster. This week's pay is in your hand.

choices.lesson: A jar with a name feels off-limits. ₹100 a month, and the goal stops being a dream.
'Whatever is left' is usually nothing. Save at the start of the month, not the end.
choices.hint: When is there ever money 'left'?

choices.lesson: 'Next month' keeps moving. Without a named goal, the money finds something else.

default.title: FRIEND IN NEED?
default.speaker: Friend
default.text: 'Lend me ₹500? I'll return it Monday, promise.' You haven't set aside your savings yet this month.

pocket_money.title: FRIEND IN NEED?
pocket_money.speaker: Imran
pocket_money.text: 'Your money came from home, na? Lend me ₹500, I'll return it Monday!' You haven't saved anything yet.

scholarship.title: FRIEND IN NEED?
scholarship.speaker: Classmate
scholarship.text: 'Allowance came, na? Lend me ₹500 till Monday!' This month's savings aren't set aside yet.

earner.title: FRIEND IN NEED?
earner.speaker: Co-worker
earner.text: 'Lend me ₹500 from your pay? Monday, pakka.' You haven't put away your savings yet.

choices.lesson: You lent before you saved. Now your plan depends on someone else's 'Monday'.
choices.hint: What happens to your savings if Monday never comes?

choices.lesson: Save first, then lend only what you could live without. That's paying yourself first.
Your savings are safe. Saying no kindly is a skill. Next time, lend only what you can spare.

default.title: EMERGENCY!
default.speaker: Bad luck
default.text: Something breaks and it costs ₹400 right now. Your next money is weeks away.

pocket_money.title: CRACKED SCREEN
pocket_money.speaker: Your phone
pocket_money.text: Your phone slips and the screen cracks. Cheapest fix at the mobile shop: ₹400. Next money is weeks away.

scholarship.title: TRIP FEE DUE
scholarship.speaker: Class teacher
scholarship.text: College trip fee: ₹400, due Friday. The next allowance is two months away.

earner.title: WORK STOPPED
earner.speaker: Dad
earner.text: Dad's work stopped for two weeks. Home needs ₹400 from you for groceries, today.

choices.lesson: This is exactly what an emergency buffer is for. No loan, no panic. Refill it next month.
Borrowing filled the gap, but next month starts ₹450 short. A buffer would have cost nothing extra.
choices.hint: Is there money set aside for exactly this?

choices.lesson: No debt, good. But now the whole month is tight. A buffer stops one shock from wrecking a month.

effects.label: It got worse and cost more

choices.lesson: Ignoring a problem doesn't make it free. It usually costs more later.
choices.hint: Will this be cheaper next month?

default.title: WHERE DOES IT LIVE?
default.speaker: Classmate
default.text: Your emergency jar finally has ₹3,000. A classmate: 'Why keep it idle? Put it in shares, it'll grow!'

pocket_money.title: IDLE MONEY?
pocket_money.speaker: Cousin
pocket_money.text: Your emergency savings reached ₹3,000! Your cousin: 'Idle money is wasted money. Put it in shares, it'll grow!'

scholarship.title: IDLE MONEY?
scholarship.speaker: Senior
scholarship.text: ₹3,000 saved from your allowance, kept for emergencies. A senior: 'Why let it sleep? Put it in shares, it'll grow!'

earner.title: IDLE MONEY?
earner.speaker: Co-worker
earner.text: ₹3,000 saved from shop pay, kept for emergencies. A co-worker: 'Why sit on it? Put it in shares, it'll grow!'

effects.label: Buffer safe in the bank, ready any day

choices.lesson: Boring on purpose: safe, and there the day something breaks. An emergency buffer's job is to be ready, not to grow.

effects.label: Shares fell 20% the week your cycle broke: sold at a loss

choices.lesson: Shares can be 20% down the very week you need the money. Emergency money stays safe and ready; only money you won't need for years should take risks.
choices.hint: What if you need it the week prices fall?

effects.label: ₹300 slipped out of the almirah on small treats

choices.lesson: It's there when you need it, but cash at home is easy to dip into and earns nothing. A bank account is just as ready, and safer.
High interest means high risk. Your emergency money became someone else's promise, and promises don't pay hospital bills.
choices.hint: Can you get it back the day you need it?

default.title: NOW OR LATER?
default.speaker: Uncle
default.text: Your uncle smiles: 'I'll give you ₹500. Do you want it today, or the same ₹500 next year?'

pocket_money.title: NOW OR LATER?
pocket_money.speaker: Uncle
pocket_money.text: Uncle visits for Sankranti: 'Here's ₹500 for you. Today, or the same ₹500 next year?'

scholarship.title: NOW OR LATER?
scholarship.speaker: Aunt
scholarship.text: Your aunt: 'Great exam results! ₹500 for you. Today, or the same ₹500 next year?'

earner.title: NOW OR LATER?
earner.speaker: Shop owner
earner.text: Shop owner: 'Good work this year. ₹500 bonus: take it now, or the same ₹500 next year?'

choices.lesson: Money today beats the same money later: it can start growing now, before prices rise.

effects.label: Uncle's ₹500 arrived, but it buys less now

choices.lesson: Same ₹500, a year later: no growth, and it buys less. That's the time value of money.
choices.hint: Will ₹500 buy the same things next year?

choices.lesson: Taking it today was right. Spending all of it was a choice; part of it could have started growing.

default.title: PRICES RISING
default.speaker: Canteen anna
default.text: 'Samosa is ₹12 now, not ₹10.' Your ₹1,000 savings sits in a tin box at home, earning nothing.

pocket_money.title: PRICES RISING
pocket_money.speaker: Canteen anna
pocket_money.intro: Mom says you can open a student account together at the bank branch.
pocket_money.text: 'Samosa is ₹12 now, not ₹10.' The ₹1,000 you saved sits in a tin box at home.

scholarship.title: PRICES RISING
scholarship.speaker: Bus conductor
scholarship.text: 'Fare went up again!' The ₹1,000 of allowance you held back sits as cash in your room.

earner.title: PRICES RISING
earner.speaker: Shop owner
earner.text: Rice and oil went up again this month. Your ₹1,000 savings sits in a tin under the counter.

choices.lesson: Prices rise every year. Money that grows can keep up; money in a tin quietly shrinks.

choices.text: KEEP IT IN THE TIN BOX
choices.lesson: The notes are safe, but inflation eats what they can buy. ₹1,000 buys less every year.
choices.hint: Samosas went from ₹10 to ₹12. What happens to your ₹1,000?

choices.lesson: Inflation is a reason to make savings grow, not to spend them all.

default.title: STALL WEEK
default.speaker: Uncle
default.text: Uncle's Charminar stall is yours for a week, with ₹1,000 for stock. Rain or shine? Nobody knows.

pocket_money.title: STALL WEEK
pocket_money.speaker: Uncle
pocket_money.intro: Bonalu week, right in the monsoon.
pocket_money.text: Uncle lets you run his Charminar stall with ₹1,000 for stock. Will it rain? The forecast is a guess.

scholarship.title: STALL WEEK
scholarship.speaker: Aunt
scholarship.text: Holiday week: your aunt lets you stock her stall near Charminar with ₹1,000. Rain or sun? Nobody knows.

earner.title: STALL WEEK
earner.speaker: Shop owner
earner.text: Your shop owner opens a festival stall at Laad Bazaar and lets you pick ₹1,000 of stock. Rain or shine?

choices.lesson: Everything on one bet: when the weather didn't play along, nothing sold.
choices.hint: What sells if it doesn't rain?

choices.lesson: Umbrellas sold in the rain, caps and water in the sun. Owning things that don't fail together is diversification.
A 'sure thing' tip is still one bet. Big hopes, big risk.
choices.hint: What if the tip is wrong?

default.title: OTP REQUEST
default.speaker: Unknown number
default.text: 'I sent my OTP to your number by mistake. Please share it back, urgent!'

pocket_money.title: OTP REQUEST
pocket_money.speaker: Unknown number
pocket_money.text: Mom's phone buzzes: 'I sent my OTP to this number by mistake. Please share it, very urgent!'

scholarship.title: COLLECT REQUEST
scholarship.speaker: UPI request
scholarship.text: A UPI request pops up: 'Receive ₹2,000 scholarship bonus. Enter your PIN to accept.'

earner.title: PIN TO RECEIVE?
earner.speaker: Customer
earner.text: A customer: 'I'm sending ₹500 for the groceries. Just approve the request with your PIN.'

choices.lesson: An OTP or PIN is a key to the account. Whoever has it can take money out. That ₹500 is gone.
choices.hint: Do you ever need a PIN to RECEIVE money?

effects.label: They kept pushing for an hour

choices.lesson: Talking to a scammer gives them time to pressure you. You don't owe them an answer.
choices.hint: Do you need to know their story?

choices.lesson: You never need a PIN or OTP to receive money, only to send it. Never share either.
Good instinct to check. And the answer is always the same: never share an OTP or PIN.

default.title: SCAM CALL
default.speaker: Caller
default.text: I'm from the scholarship office. Pay ₹500 now or your money is cancelled!

pocket_money.title: SCAM CALL
pocket_money.speaker: 'Electricity office'
pocket_money.text: A caller on Mom's phone: 'Your bill is unpaid. Pay ₹500 on this link now or power is cut tonight!'

scholarship.title: SCAM CALL
scholarship.speaker: 'ePASS officer'
scholarship.text: Your allowance is approved! Pay a ₹500 processing fee now or it lapses today.

earner.title: SCAM CALL
earner.speaker: 'Bank officer'
earner.text: 'Your UPI will be blocked today! Pay a ₹500 KYC fee on this link to keep it active.'

choices.lesson: Real offices never demand instant payment on a call or a link. That ₹500 is gone.
choices.hint: Would a real office rush you on a phone call?

choices.lesson: Friends guess. The official portal knows.
Safe. Even safer: check the official site so you know for sure.
You verified at the source. That's the whole trick against scams.

default.title: EASY MONEY JOB
default.speaker: Group admin
default.text: 'Like 3 videos, earn ₹150!' It paid once. Now: 'Deposit ₹500 to unlock VIP tasks: ₹5,000 a day!'

pocket_money.title: EASY MONEY JOB
pocket_money.speaker: Group admin
pocket_money.text: A chat group paid you ₹150 for liking videos. Now: 'Pay ₹500 to unlock VIP tasks, earn ₹5,000 a day!'

scholarship.title: EASY MONEY JOB
scholarship.speaker: Group admin
scholarship.text: 'Part-time job for students!' It paid ₹150 for likes. Now: 'Deposit ₹500 for VIP tasks, ₹5,000 a day!'

earner.title: EASY MONEY JOB
earner.speaker: 'Recruiter'
earner.text: 'Rate shops online, earn ₹5,000 a day!' The first ₹150 really came. Now they want ₹500 'to unlock'.

choices.lesson: The first ₹150 was bait. No real job asks you to pay to work. ₹5,000 a day for likes is too good to be true.
choices.hint: Why would a real job need YOUR money first?

choices.lesson: Testing a scam with 'a little' money is still paying a scammer. They always ask for more.
choices.hint: Is a small payment to a scammer safe?

choices.lesson: Safe. Reporting it too helps stop them reaching your friends.
Real jobs pay you; they never charge you. 1930, the national cyber-fraud helpline, can now warn others.
